headline: Diplomatic Visit Results in Local Chaii-Walla Receiving 'Strategic Defensive Supplies' Including One Industrial-Grade Strainer
body:
"I was expecting a tax inspector, but instead I got three guys in dark suits who handed me a military-spec tea filter and told me my stall is now a 'critical infrastructure point' for the neighborhood," said a local tea vendor operating in South Delhi.

"Honestly, I appreciate the gesture, but this titanium strainer is so heavy that my arm aches by the third cup, even if it does technically prevent the infusion of unauthorized chai leaves," remarked a regular office-commuter waiting for his morning caffeine fix.

"The government said this was about global defense solidarity, but I just watched the vendor try to fit a surplus radar antenna on top of his biscuit jar to improve the stall's 'defensive posture'," observed a local college student witnessing the installation.

"If the goal was to secure our infrastructure against the morning rush, they should have just given us an extra stove and a larger gas cylinder, not a reinforced helmet for the person washing the cups," laughed a nearby newspaper hawker.

"They told me if the quality of my cutting chai drops, it would be considered a breach of international logistics, so I have officially upgraded to a high-capacity iron kettle for the sake of global stability," noted the tea stall owner.
caption: From kitchen essentials to global defense, the scale of diplomatic aid has never been more confusing. Are we ready for the new age of tea-stall security? #Diplomacy #ChaiTime #GlobalAffairs #StrategicStrainer (satire)
igHook: Would you trust a military-grade strainer with your morning chai?
imagePrompt: A close-up, photorealistic shot of an ordinary, weathered roadside tea stall counter cluttered with glasses, a biscuit jar, and a noticeably out-of-place, high-tech, reinforced metal tea strainer resting on a worn wooden table.

It maintains a deadpan, affectionate tone, uses specific local references (South Delhi, cutting chai), and avoids the repetitive 'shipping junk to Ukraine' formula that plagued the rest of the batch.
